brief.headline: Offer to pay them 15 days faster in exchange for a 6% price cut — their cash is stuck for 101 days (vs 64 for peers) and they borrow at 12.16%, so early payment is worth that much to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 6% price cut if we pay 15 days earlier
priceAsk.target: Around ₹235–240/kg (down from the ₹250/kg typical market line)
priceAsk.basis: Market research shows pharma/ORS sachet laminates ask ₹205–305/kg, typically ₹250/kg — we're at the top of the fair band. Their borrowing rate is 12.16%, so paying 15 days early is worth ~6% annualized to them. We free up ₹26.60 L for ourselves and they get cash 15 days sooner when their cash is stuck for 101 days.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt, in exchange for the 6% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: This costs us ₹26.60 L in cash (we pay sooner), but we save roughly that amount through the price cut, and we strengthen a supplier who's cash-tight.

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath Roto's revenue is ₹1064.86 Cr and we spend ₹6.47 Cr with them — we're 0.61% of their sales, so a mid-sized account. They keep only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, so there's little room for a straight price squeeze. But their cash is stuck for 101 days vs 64 days at similar firms, and they borrow money at 12.16% — so paying them faster is genuinely valuable to them. They also owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr debt), and there's an EPF payment delay flag, so supply risk is real if we push too hard on price alone. The trade — faster payment for a price cut — is fair to both sides.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than peers
They borrow at a high rate
Very thin profit — a big price cut could hurt supply
Credit rating is middling and there's an EPF delay flag
evidence.figure: CARE BBB+ / Stable, EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — proven and scalable for laminate sachets (₹2758.00 Cr revenue, health C 59/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health C 46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of global Constantia group, focuses on pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D 31/100).

risks: Their credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable and they show EPF payment delays — watch supply continuity and don't push so hard on price that we tip them over.
Debt is 1.25 times their equity and interest coverage is only 1.94x — a financial wobble could disrupt our supply.
We have no internal price benchmark (no other laminate supplier in our data) — the ₹205–305/kg market band is our only external anchor, so verify it with a second quote.
Their Altman Z-score is 2.36 (grey zone, between safe and distress) — keep Huhtamaki or UFLEX warm as a backup and don't concentrate all our laminate volume here.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 15-day payment terms and in return we're looking for a 6% price reduction — paying you faster frees up cash for you, and the saving covers our own cash cost.
